Lenskart, Meesho add $394 million to SoftBank's portfolio value in September quarter
Lenskart's fair value rose 31 percent during the quarter, while Meesho's increased 17 percent, as both companies reported revenue growth and improving profitability metrics.
Moneycontrol News
November 10, 2026 / 19:18 IST
Lenskart, Meesho add $394 million to SoftBank's portfolio value in September quarter
Lenskart and Meesho together added nearly $400 million to the value of SoftBank's public investment portfolio in the September quarter, with the two Indian companies emerging as among the Japanese investor's biggest contributors to portfolio gains.
According to SoftBank Group's Q2 FY26 investor presentation, the fair value of its Lenskart investment increased by $273 million during the quarter ended September 30, while Meesho added another $121 million. Both investments are held through SoftBank Vision Fund 2 (SVF2).
Lenskart's investment was valued at $900 million at the end of the quarter, while Meesho's stood at $800 million. Their combined quarterly increase of $394 million came despite an overall decline in the fair value of SoftBank's public investment portfolio.
SoftBank reported a $900 million decline in the quarterly fair value of its public investments, which had an aggregate unrealised fair value of $20.1 billion as of September 30. Gains from the two Indian companies were offset by declines in several other portfolio holdings.
Lenskart recorded a 31% increase in its stock price during the quarter, while Meesho's shares rose 17%, according to the presentation.

The gains also coincided with improvements in the companies' operating performance. Lenskart's first-quarter revenue grew 34% year-on-year, while its EBITDA rose 95% and profit after tax increased by more than 180%.
Meesho reported 34% year-on-year revenue growth, while its losses narrowed 68% on the back of improving margins and operational efficiencies, SoftBank said.
The gains underline the contribution of the two Indian internet companies to SoftBank's portfolio following their public market debuts. However, the increase in fair value should not be confused with cash profits realised by the investor.
SoftBank's quarterly fair-value calculations include realised and unrealised gains and losses from public investments, along with dividends and other income. The figures are before taxes and expenses.
The investor's public portfolio comprised 44 companies as of September 30, with an aggregate unrealised fair value of $20.1 billion. This represented 11% of the combined funds' total unrealised fair value, according to the presentation.
